main_topics.reason: The user came because pelvic pain returned three months after surgery and described its pattern and asked if recurrence this fast is normal.
The opening question was whether another surgery is needed, and the user later asked when surgery would be considered.
Several turns covered post-surgery hormonal management, with the user asking specifically about the hormonal IUD and mood effects.
The user explained that the pill caused low mood and no libido and did not want to return to it.
The user said they felt defeated and later said they felt less hopeless about surgery forever.
The user engaged with the new idea that not all pain is endometriosis, but it was a short exchange.
The user mentioned in one line they were told to come back if problems and given no treatment.
The user did not know they could request it and accepted it as a good idea.

output.summary: A user three months after a laparoscopy for endometriosis reported returning cyclical pelvic pain and feared needing more surgery. The bot explained post-surgical hormonal options such as a hormonal IUD given the user's poor tolerance of the pill, when repeat surgery is considered, and possible muscular pain, then gave a three-step plan. The user said it was clear and that they felt less like it was surgery forever.
